review.description: Reviewed maintain-flow-contracts S1-S5. S3/S4/S5 retain owned verification, literal inherited paths, failure cleanup and native graph ordering while exporting each Make process ownership fields as one complete private batch. Hosted verification is allowed 60 minutes; no suite or assertion is removed, and historical adoption and open gaps remain unchanged.
review.implementation: Makefile now calls --make-owner-fields once per native Make process and rejects an empty export before work. make_owner.fields writes all six fixed fields with legacy CRLF framing into a 0700 batch using 0600 files under the live owner directory-FD alias; it returns the alias only after successful closes and removes partial batches on failure. The legacy field endpoint remains. local_verification pins the reviewed prologue; verification_run dispatches the new endpoint.
review.tests: test_make_exports_ownership_with_one_batch_per_make_process exercises the real caller/worker graph and retains shared preparation/order assertions while requiring exactly two batched exports and no legacy calls. MakeOwnerFieldTests asserts hostile raw bytes, exact field set, directory/file modes, legacy equivalence and controlled fifth-write cleanup. Existing hostile TMPDIR, re-exec/nested clients, stdin remake, readiness rejection and owner-death tests passed focused execution. HostedCITests asserts the 60-minute deadline. Fixture benchmarks are evidence of overhead reduction only, not new product or real-host acceptance.
